newsitem.title: CHINA: China says launches communications satellite.
newsitem.headline: China says launches communications satellite.

text.p: China on Monday said it had successfully launched into orbit a domestic telecommunications satellite after a string of launch failures last year.

A Long March 3A rocket, built by China Great Wall Industries Corp, put the satellite into orbit after a launch early on Monday morning in southwestern Xichang, a spokeswoman for the China Aerospace Corp said by telephone.
"The rocket launch was entirely successful," the spokeswoman said. "(We) are currently continuing to track the satellite."

Industry sources said last week that the launch of the Dongfanghong-3 communications satellite had been rescheduled from May 5 because China's space authorities wanted to be sure that all would go well.
China has worked to restore its reputation as a cheap but reliable launcher after suffering two high-profile launch failures in 1996.

The US$230 million Intelsat 708 satellite was lost in February 1996 after its rocket veered off course and exploded, killing six people. In August another satellite was stranded in a useless orbit after launch.
